"Patrick (Malone Quantitative)" <mal...@malonequantitative.com>: Jul 22 08:04AM -0400

It is likely that your model is underidentified, especially with only
two indicators per factor, and those categorical. In particular,
phase_1 is probably not identified. Try constraining the two phase
variables to measurement invariance (loadings and thresholds).
std.lv=TRUE is also probably not what you want for longitudinal data.
 
Pat

"Patrick (Malone Quantitative)" <mal...@malonequantitative.com>: Jul 22 09:43AM -0400

Measurement invariance for categorical indicators is most commonly
defined as loading and threshold invariance simultaneously.
 
So loadings looks something like this:
 
phase_0 =~ 1*CHRONO_0 + l1*getup_0
phase_1 =~ 1*CHRONO_1 + l1*getup_1
 
That still may not identify it, depending on other details--there
might need to be some additional constraints on l1.
 
I don't have a lot of experience with manipulating thresholds in
lavaan, but they use a | syntax for each ordinal variable. Online
tutorials or someone else here should be able to help with that
syntax.
 
Pat
 
 
--

Right now the best recommendation with lavaan would be to use the indicator product terms.
1. You create mean center indicator product terms, or residualized indicator product terms. Can use the function indProd() from semTools for this
2. Include these indicator product terms into the latent regression in lavaan reacting a new Interaction factor defined by the product indicators
3. Run the latent regression with the Latent interaction terms, this way you can evaluate the interaction regression slope, and increase in R2 by adding it
4. Probe simple intercepts and slopes for the interactions, can use the probe2WayRC (for the residualize indicators) or probe2WayMC (for the mean center indicators), functions from semTools
5. Plot the simple slopes to visualize the effect of the interactions, with plotProbe function from semTools

In the helps page of each function you can see examples

Right now the best recommendation with lavaan would be to use the indicator product terms.
1. You create mean center indicator product terms, or residualized indicator product terms. Can use the function indProd() from semTools for this

tutorials or someone else here should be able to help with that
